title: Sunset: session-stateful-v1 endpoint and migrate clients to stateless-conversation API
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: PRD: retire the legacy session-stateful-v1 endpoint (used by long-lived session clients) and migrate customers to the stateless-conversation API that provides explicit conversation IDs and server-side session token helpers. This ticket defines the migration requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout timeline, and client guidance to minimize customer disruption.
background: The session-stateful-v1 endpoint was introduced as an early experiment to handle long-lived sessions with implicit server-side state. Over time it has become a source of operational complexity: inconsistent KV cache semantics, harder routing across Dedicated pools, and ambiguous rollback semantics. The stateless-conversation API provides clearer semantics, better caching, and aligns with our unified routing and fallback logic. This PRD defines a coordinated deprecation path that prioritizes customer safety and observability.
goals: 1) Safely retire session-stateful-v1 with <6 weeks of targeted migration support per customer. 2) Ensure parity for common flows (chat continuity, attachments/pinned metadata, streaming) via stateless-conversation API. 3) Provide SDK shims, migration CLI, and automated telemetry gates to prevent user-visible regressions.
non_goals: 1) Re-architecting the conversation model beyond parity (deferred to convo-v2). 2) Supporting custom legacy session storage for >12 months. 3) Forcing on-prem customers to upgrade runtime; Private customers will receive an alternate upgrade plan.
success_metrics: 1) 90% of active session-stateful-v1 traffic migrated within 12 weeks of announcement. 2) Customer-error-rate for migrated clients <= prior baseline + 0.5% within 14 days. 3) No irrevocable data loss incidents. 4) SDK adoption: >=75% of affected active keys updated to patched SDK within 8 weeks.
stakeholders: PM: Aisha Kumar; Engineering Leads: Ethan Blake (runtime), Nina Patel (api-gateway); DX/SDK: Marco Silva; Design: Priya Rao; Support/CS: Daniel Ortiz; Legal & Security: Serena Wu
scope_included: 1) Production deprecation plan and timeline. 2) Migration playbook and client-facing docs. 3) SDK shim that translates session-stateful-v1 calls to stateless-conversation (best-effort) with deprecation warnings. 4) Telemetry dashboards and regression alerts. 5) Backwards-compatibility tests and canary plan.
scope_excluded: 1) Conversational model changes beyond mapping semantics. 2) On-prem runtime upgrades (separate Private deployment plan). 3) Creating third-party migration tools beyond the SDK shim and migration CLI.
requirements: 1) Public announcement docs and migration guide published at least 90 days before hard-deprecation. 2) SDK patch release (JS, Python, Go) with automatic shim and opt-out flag. 3) Migration CLI that can bulk-rewrite customer integrations and surface unsupported patterns. 4) Telemetry: per-key breakdown of legacy vs stateless calls, regression guards, alerting triage runbooks. 5) Canary traffic policy and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if migration increases latency beyond SLOs.
migration_steps: 1) Week 0: Draft announcement + internal playbook. 2) Week 1-4: SDK shim alpha, internal testing with partner customers. 3) Week 5: Public docs + migration repo + support runbook. 4) Week 6-12: Assisted migrations for top 20 customers (support + SE). 5) Week 13: Start rolling traffic cutover policy (soft-deprecation: 429s with guidance header for legacy patterns). 6) Week 17: Hard-deprecation for new tokens (reject new session-stateful-v1 token exchanges). 7) Week 20: Full enforcement (403/410) for remaining traffic after final notices.
acceptance_criteria: SDK shim published in JS, Python, Go with migration CLI and documented opt-out flag
Migration guide published in Confluence + public docs; includes code samples for common patterns (streaming, attachments, session pinning)
Telemetry shows migration progress per customer; dashboards deployed and accessible to Support and PMs
Canary runs demonstrate no more than 5% median latency regression for migrated flows under production load
Top 20 enterprise customers have migration plans and assigned SE/support contacts
Legal and security confirm documentation and messaging meet contractual obligations (SLA/notice windows)
rollback_criteria: If during canary or early enforcement we observe: 1) customer error-rate delta > 2% for >30m for a single customer, or 2) platform-wide availability impact >0.5% for >30m, we must pause enforcement, revert any gateway-level blocking, and engage incident runbook. Rollback requires a signed go/no-go from PM, Eng runtime lead, and CS lead.
telemetry_gates: 1) Pre-enforcement: baseline measurement of session-stateful-v1 error-rate, latency P50/P95, and per-key traffic. 2) During migration: automated alerts if any key breaches error delta >1% or P95 latency increase >250ms. 3) Post-enforcement: daily migration health for first 14 days and weekly thereafter.
support_and_se_plan: 1) Prepare canned migration emails and in-product banners for affected keys. 2) Dedicated migration slack channel and office hours during weeks 5-12. 3) SEs assigned to top 20 accounts and a triage rota for high-severity failures.
communication_plan: 1) Public blog + email announcement (90d). 2) In-console banner for affected projects (60d). 3) Targeted outreach to enterprise customers with migration kits (30d). 4) Final warning emails at 14d and 3d before enforcement.
engineering_work_items: ENG-2210: SDK shim implementation; ENG-3345: Gateway deprecation mode and header schema; ENG-4021: Telemetry dashboards and migration metrics; ENG-5210: Canary orchestration for traffic steering
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hidden integrations using server-side stateful semantics (attachments or pinned metadata) may break. Mitigation: SDK shim attempts best-effort behavior, migration CLI flags unmatched patterns, and Support/SEs handle manual migrations for affected customers. Risk: Private/on-prem customers may delay upgrades. Mitigation: Separate Private upgrade track and contractual exceptions with clear expiry dates.
qa_and_validation: 1) End-to-end tests for chat continuity, streaming resume, and attachment retrieval. 2) Load tests to validate canary thresholds with traffic shapes representative of top-10 customers. 3) User acceptance testing with 3 pilot customers before public docs release.
post_mortem_and_follow_up: After enforcement, run a 30-day postmortem covering migration velocity, customer incidents, and SDK adoption. Action items from the postmortem will be tracked and prioritized in the API Consolidation project backlog.
notes: Keep migration messaging explicit about data retention and session export options. Offer a 'session export' tool if customers request historical continuity. Coordinate with Billing for any contract-adjusted migration assistance.
